Everyone at work had a meeting today, including one of my managers, Tim (name changed for privacy). The meeting leaders were setting up a presentation for us, which was going to be shown through a web browser. They used Internet Explorer, but it crashed at one point. Two coworkers among us spectators recommended Google Chrome, but I thought it would be fun to recommend Firefox, instead.

Tim: Did you seriously just say Firefox?
Me: Uh, yeah.
Tim: Why would you use Firefox?
Me: What's wrong with Firefox?
Tim: You do know that Firefox is just like Internet Explorer?
Me: What? No, it's not.
Tim: Yeah, it is. Firefox uses Internet Explorer.
Me: What are you talking about?
Tim: Firefox is just Internet Explorer, but with a different interface.
I was taken aback from the sheer ignorance. I then regathered my thoughts.
Me: You're wrong. Firefox is its own open source project, whereas Internet Explorer is closed-source and proprietary. They don't even use the same layout engines.
Tim: Believe me. They're the same thing.
Me: Well, I've done my own research and I believe that more than I do you.
Tim: Okay.

What a hilarious exchange. Is this why he antagonizes Firefox whenever a customer mentions it? C'mon, bro. Do your research.
Apparently, Firefox is just IE with a UI skin, according to Tim.
Is it possible to slap Tim with a fish?

Sounds like a manager, for sure ;)

Did the guys in the room back you up at all?

Even on the Internet, it's hard to find anyone who likes Firefox.
